calibration_constraint: Distinguish acute consolidation-supporting activity (session-scale) from systems consolidation outcome (weeks-to-years); architectural claims for consolidation outcome < 0.40

mechanism_chain.process: During quiet wakefulness and sleep, hippocampal sharp-wave ripple complexes (SWRs) reactivate recent spatial experiences in compressed temporal sequence
mechanism_chain.substrate: CA3 → CA1 sharp-wave ripples (150–250 Hz, 50–120 ms); coupled with cortical slow oscillations and sleep spindles

data.finding: Sharp-wave ripple complexes (150-250 Hz, 50-120 ms) occur during quiet wakefulness and NREM sleep; they reactivate recent spatial experiences in compressed temporal sequence
data.effect: SWRs compress replay of recent experience

data.finding: Place cells active during navigation replay in same sequence during subsequent SWRs, compressed ~20× relative to real time

justification.backing: Buzsáki's work established SWRs as the primary hippocampal oscillation for memory consolidation. The compressed replay during SWRs provides the mechanism for transferring recent experiences to neocortical long-term storage.
justification.qualifier: The SWR mechanism is well-established in rodents. Human evidence relies on indirect measures (scalp EEG does not resolve individual SWRs) and fMRI signatures of hippocampal-cortical connectivity.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if human hippocampus uses different consolidation mechanisms than rodents; but indirect evidence supports SWR-like activity in human hippocampus.

mechanism_chain.process: SWR-mediated replay transfers spatial information from hippocampal to neocortical storage: repeated replay strengthens cortico-cortical connections that encode the spatial schema independently of hippocampus
mechanism_chain.substrate: Hippocampal → entorhinal → neocortical (mPFC, posterior parietal) transfer via SWR-spindle-slow oscillation coupling

data.finding: SWRs are temporally coupled with cortical slow oscillations and sleep spindles; this coupling is the substrate for hippocampal → neocortical transfer
Disrupting SWRs during rest impairs memory consolidation; the replay is necessary for transfer

justification.backing: The standard model of systems consolidation holds that repeated SWR replay gradually strengthens neocortical connections, eventually enabling memory retrieval without hippocampal involvement. The causal role of SWRs is demonstrated by disruption studies.
justification.qualifier: The transfer mechanism is established; the timescale for architectural spatial memories to become hippocampal-independent is uncertain (weeks to months).
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if consolidation occurs through mechanisms other than SWR replay; but disruption studies support the necessity of SWRs for spatial memory consolidation.

mechanism_chain.process: Schema availability accelerates transfer: when neocortical schema already exists, new hippocampal spatial information is integrated into schema faster (days rather than weeks)
mechanism_chain.source: Tse et al. (2007); Tse et al. (2011)

data.finding: With pre-existing schema, new spatial information shows neocortical expression within 24-48 hours rather than weeks
mPFC lesions impair schema-dependent accelerated consolidation; mPFC is necessary for schema effects

justification.backing: Morris and colleagues demonstrated that schemas fundamentally accelerate consolidation. When a spatial schema exists, new information can reach stable neocortical representation in days rather than the weeks typically required for slow consolidation.
justification.qualifier: The acceleration effect is demonstrated in rodents with laboratory-constructed schemas. Human architectural schemas are naturalistic and may show different acceleration dynamics.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if human architectural schemas are too variable to support consistent acceleration; but the general schema mechanism is robust.

mechanism_chain.process: Architectural environment supports or impedes acute consolidation-supporting activity (SWR replay, DMN re-engagement) through environmental conditions (see MS_RIPPLE_REPLAY_002)
mechanism_chain.substrate: Environmental modulation of hippocampal state transitions (theta → LIA/SWR)

data.finding: SWR generation requires transition from theta state (active exploration) to LIA state (quiet wakefulness); environmental conditions that maintain theta suppress SWRs
Rest periods with low cognitive demand show increased hippocampal-cortical connectivity that predicts subsequent memory

justification.backing: The architectural bridge is that environments supporting quiet wakefulness (low arousal, minimal cognitive demand, absence of threat) enable the hippocampal state transition from theta to LIA that is necessary for SWR generation.
justification.qualifier: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT: the causal chain from architectural feature → hippocampal state transition → SWR generation is inferred rather than directly demonstrated. The mechanism is plausible but the specific environmental modulation is untested.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if human hippocampal state transitions are less sensitive to environmental conditions than rodent hippocampus; or if cognitive factors dominate environmental factors.

exposure_duration.interpretation: Architectural rest spaces support SWR replay and DMN re-engagement during the same session as spatial learning. This is acute consolidation-SUPPORTING activity, not consolidation itself.

memory_consolidation.interpretation: Confidence that any single architectural design choice meaningfully affects the OUTCOME of systems consolidation is low, because the causal chain from architectural feature → acute replay → repeated replay → neocortical transfer is too long and involves too many non-architectural variables

hippocampal_encoding.interpretation: When a neocortical schema exists, systems consolidation is accelerated: new spatial information becomes schema-integrated within days rather than weeks (Tse et al., 2011)

age_group.effect: SWR frequency and amplitude decline with age; coupling between SWRs, spindles, and slow oscillations degrades. Systems consolidation is slower in older adults.
age_group.mechanism: Age-related decline in hippocampal interneuron function (Mander et al., 2013)

memory_consolidation.effect: Chronic sleep disruption (common in hospitals, shift-work environments) severely impairs the SWR-spindle-slow oscillation coupling that drives systems consolidation

IC2_AX4_interaction.IC2_body_budget: Body budget deficit disrupts sleep architecture, reducing the SWR-spindle-slow oscillation coupling that drives consolidation. Chronic allostatic load is a primary enemy of systems consolidation.
IC2_AX4_interaction.AX4_perceived_control: Low perceived control elevates cortisol, which impairs hippocampal neuroplasticity and reduces the quality of SWR replay. The chronic stress pathway (AX4 → cortisol → hippocampal atrophy) is the primary route through which environmental control loss impairs long-term memory consolidation.

cross_template_references: MS_RIPPLE_REPLAY_002 — provides the acute consolidation-supporting activity parameters
STRESS-I T6 — cortisol impairs consolidation-supporting neural activity
MS_CONSOLIDATION_RESTORATION_001 — DMN-mediated integration complements SWR replay

spatial_configuration.interpretation: Presence of consolidation-permissive rest spaces (per MS_RIPPLE_REPLAY_002 conditions) in proximity to learning zones supports acute consolidation activity

repeated_exposure_to_same_space.interpretation: Repeated navigation of the same spatial layout across sessions provides the repeated SWR replay substrate for gradual consolidation

name: Systems Consolidation and Hippocampal-Neocortical Transfer
